_schema.note: The readiness board. Spent BEFORE the attack starts, which is the entire commercial argument expressed as a mechanic: resilience is a set of decisions already made, not a set of reactions available on the night.

rules.budget: how many points the player has to spend
rules.maxPerPillar: cap per pillar. Set below budget on purpose — it makes a single-product build impossible to express, so the player discovers the layering argument by trying to break it.

card.id: slug. Also the engine's switch key, so do not rename one without grepping for it.
card.product: the real N-able product this capability belongs to
card.name: the capability, in the language a security team would use
card.desc: what it is, in the world
card.effect: what it does in the run, stated plainly enough that the player can plan around it
card.recap: past tense, for the result screen. Reads as a decision the player made months ago.

cards.name: Enforced patch window
cards.desc: Every endpoint and server patched on a schedule nobody can defer, with exceptions that expire.
cards.effect: BlackVault starts every stage further back, and a breach costs one point of damage instead of two.
cards.recap: You closed known entry points on a schedule, so the attack started from further out and every mistake cost you less.

cards.name: Complete asset inventory
cards.desc: Every device, account and service accounted for, reconciled against what is approved.
cards.effect: A stage you only slow down costs the estate nothing at all.
cards.recap: You knew exactly what every box was and what depended on it, so the near-misses cost you nothing.

cards.name: 24/7 monitored response
cards.desc: Analysts watching the estate on the hours nobody on the payroll is awake for.
cards.effect: Three free scans, and BlackVault moves slower until you commit.
cards.recap: Somebody was already engaging at 04:00, so you were never the first to know and never the only one working.

cards.name: Automated host isolation
cards.desc: A host that behaves like a compromised host comes off the network without waiting for a human.
cards.effect: The first breach of the run is downgraded to mitigated.
cards.recap: Automated isolation caught your first mistake before a person could have.

cards.name: Immutable off-site vault
cards.desc: Restore points that cannot be edited or deleted by anyone, including you, until they expire.
cards.effect: Backups can never be lost — and while they stand, the business does not close.
cards.recap: Your restore points could not be deleted by a credential, which is why you still had a business.

cards.name: Tested restore runbook
cards.desc: A documented restore, rehearsed quarterly, with a measured time to first system back.
cards.effect: Any stage BlackVault does not get through brings a system all the way back. A perfect stack brings two.
cards.recap: You had restored before under no pressure, so systems came back to service during the incident rather than part-way back after it.
